newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Lagos bomb blast wounds 12 soldiers, radio.
newsitem.headline: Lagos bomb blast wounds 12 soldiers, radio.

text.p: A bomb blast rocked the centre of Nigeria's biggest city Lagos on Wednesday critically injuring 12 soldiers, an independent radio station reported.
Ray Power radio said the explosion in the Alausa district damaged a city corporation bus carrying the soldiers and caused pandemonium in the residential area.
"The injured soldiers are being carried into a commercial bus and there is still blood all over the place," a Ray Power radio reporter said from the scene.
She said the bomb was apparently planted in a refuse dump and the explosion was heard all round the vicinity.
"Walls of some homes have been damaged and some people hit by flying glass," one said on the radio.

On Monday, a time-bomb exploded within the same area injuring three people in an attack that was aimed at Lagos state military administrator Colonel Muhammed Marwa, a close aide of military ruler General Sani Abacha.
Police say eight people have been arrested over that explosion, which follows a string of similar blasts in politically volatile Nigeria.
They say the Monday bomb had a striking resemblance to one last month that killed three people, including the head of airport security, in a bungled car bomb explosion in Lagos.
Police said the victims were agents of exiled opposition leader and Nobel prize winner for literature, Wole Soyinka.
No one has so far claimed responsibility for the attacks.
Nigeria plunged into crisis in 1993 when the previous military government annulled a presidential election that would have restored civil rule.
Abacha seized power in the chaos that ensued and has pledged to hand over to a democratically elected president in 1998 but his critics say his agenda is to hang on to power.

The U.S. State Department said on Tuesday it had received information that bomb attacks might take place at Nigerian airports during the last two weeks of December and warned Americans travelling to the country to be cautious.
A public announcement did not say where the information came from, or provide further details.

"There is no indication of a threat directed against American citizens," the announcement said. "However, Americans in or travelling to Nigeria should exercise caution and report suspicious activity to the local police or the American embassy."
